DECODE function with even number of arguments produces incorrect CASE statement

When using the DECODE function with an even number of arguments (no default value), the parser incorrectly generates a CASE statement with a default clause instead of no default.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import sqlglot

# This should generate a CASE statement without ELSE clause
sql = "SELECT DECODE(a, 1, 'one')"
parsed = sqlglot.parse_one(sql)
result = parsed.sql()
print("Result:", result)
print("Expected: SELECT CASE WHEN a = 1 THEN 'one' END")

# Another example
sql2 = "SELECT DECODE(a, 1, 'one', 2, 'two')" 
parsed2 = sqlglot.parse_one(sql2)
result2 = parsed2.sql()
print("Result:", result2)
print("Expected: SELECT CASE WHEN a = 1 THEN 'one' WHEN a = 2 THEN 'two' END")
```

The issue occurs because when there's an even number of expressions in DECODE (meaning no default value should be present), the parser still adds the last expression as a default clause in the generated CASE statement.
</issue>
